words.gloss: of cat, camel, wolf, boar, dog, sheep, dvāgulī, naptṛ, crow, owl

hindi: बिल्ली, ऊँट, भेड़िया, सूअर, कुत्ता, भेड़, द्वागुली, नप्तृ, कौआ और उल्लू के, अथवा रात में विचरने वाले अन्य प्राणियों के, एक के, दो के या बहुतों के, दाहिने और बाएँ नेत्र लेकर दो भागों में चूर्ण बनवाए।
english: Having taken the right and left eyes of cats, camels, wolves, boars, dogs, sheep, dvāgulīs, naptṛs, crows and owls, or of other night-roaming creatures, of one, of two, or of many, one should have a powder made in two parts.

text_flags.why: possible: the creature is called vāgulī in units 6 and 17; the initial d may be a typing slip (the Devanagari has the same द्वा)

notes: dvāgulī and naptṛ are obscure creature names and are kept as printed (naptṛ literally 'grandson'); not identified. dvāgulī is possibly a variant of vāgulī (see flag). dvidhā cūrṇam: 'powder in two parts'; the next unit suggests right and left eyes are powdered separately, but the line does not say so. The e-text marks compound members with '.' and the unsandhied join ca-akṣīṇi with '-'.

hindi: फिर दाहिने को बाएँ से और बाएँ को दाहिने से लेपित करके वह रात में और अँधेरे में देखता है।
english: Then, having anointed the right [eye] with the left [powder] and the left with the right, he sees at night and in darkness.
notes: Only 'the right' and 'the left' are in the Sanskrit; eyes and powders are supplied from the previous unit. The subject of paśyati is not stated.

hindi: एक आम्लक, वराह की आँख, जुगनू, काली शारिवा। इससे जिसकी आँखें लेपित हैं, वह रात में रूपों को देखता है।
english: One āmlaka, a boar's eye, a firefly, black śārivā. One whose eyes are anointed with this sees forms at night.
notes: Ingredient list in the nominative. āmlaka (possibly a fruit or a sour thing) and śārivā are kept as names and not identified. eka-āmlakaṃ could also be read eka + āmlakaṃ 'one, an āmlaka', same sense. kha-dyota = 'sky-light', the usual word for firefly. kāla-śārivā: kāla taken as 'black'.

hindi: तीन रात उपवास किया हुआ, पुष्य में, शस्त्र से मारे गए अथवा शूल में पिरोए गए पुरुष की खोपड़ी में, मिट्टी में जौ बोकर, भेड़ के दूध से सींचे।
english: Having fasted three nights, under Puṣya, one should sow barley in earth in the skull of a man killed by a weapon or impaled on a stake, and sprinkle it with sheep's milk.

text_flags.why: possible: āvāpya 'having sown' fits barley (yavān) and the earth; āvāsya (ā-√vas or ā-√vā) gives no clear sense

notes: Puṣya is a lunar mansion (nakṣatra); inst. puṣyeṇa taken as 'under/at Puṣya'. 'sow it in earth in the skull' is the literal order; 'it' in the English is the sown barley. If āvāsya is kept, the sense is unclear ('having made them stay'). The whole recipe is given as a bare description; no effect is claimed in this unit.

hindi: तब जौ के अंकुरों की माला बाँधकर, जिसका छाया-रूप नष्ट हो गया है ऐसा वह विचरता है।
english: Then, having tied on a garland of sprouted barley, he moves about with his shadow-form lost.
notes: naṣṭac.chāyā.rūpaś is split naṣṭa-chāyā-rūpaḥ (the e-text has the sandhi cc inside a '.' compound; unit 13 prints naṣṭa.chāyā.rūpaś). chāyā-rūpa 'shadow-form' is kept literal; it may be read 'shadow and form' (dvandva) or 'appearance'; the meaning 'invisible' is not stated in the text. virūḍha = grown, sprouted.

words.gloss: of dog, cat, owl and vāgulī

hindi: तीन रात उपवास किया हुआ, पुष्य में, कुत्ते, बिल्ली, उल्लू और वागुली की दाहिनी और बाईं आँखों का दो भागों में चूर्ण बनवाए।
english: Having fasted three nights, under Puṣya, one should have a powder made in two parts of the right and left eyes of dogs, cats, owls and vāgulīs.

text_flags.why: short a for ā: rātra is spelt with ā in units 4, 8, 10 and 28; the Devanagari also has रत्र

notes: vāgulī is an obscure creature name, kept as printed (possibly bat, not stated). The 'right and left eyes' are of the four creatures named.

hindi: तब अपने ढंग से जिसकी आँखें लेपित हैं और जिसका छाया-रूप नष्ट हो गया है, वह विचरता है।
english: Then, with his eyes anointed in his own way and his shadow-form lost, he moves about.
notes: yathā-svam is literally 'according to one's own'; it may mean each powder in its own way (each eye-powder as prescribed) or 'as he himself wishes'. Kept general.

hindi: तीन रात उपवास किया हुआ, पुष्य में, पुरुष का वध करने वाले काण्डक की शलाका और अञ्जनी बनवाए।
english: Having fasted three nights, under Puṣya, one should have made a rod and an añjanī of a man-killing kāṇḍaka.
notes: kāṇḍaka is obscure (it could be an arrow or reed-like object; not stated) and is kept as a name. The genitive kāṇḍakasya may govern only śalākām or both objects; 'of' is placed before both. añjanī = a vessel or stick for eye ointment (añjana).

hindi: तब किसी एक नेत्र-चूर्ण से जिसकी आँखें लेपित हैं, वह नष्ट-छाया-रूप होकर विचरता है।
english: Then, with his eyes anointed with any one of the eye-powders, he moves about with his shadow-form lost.
notes: tato anyatamena: tataḥ is written tato; no avagraha in the e-text. 'the eye-powders' refers back to the powders made in units 1 to 6 (supplied from context).

hindi: तीन रात उपवास किया हुआ, पुष्य में, काले लोहे की अञ्जनी और शलाका बनवाए।
english: Having fasted three nights, under Puṣya, one should have an añjanī and a rod of black iron made.
notes: kālāyasīm = kāla-ayasīm 'black-iron' (feminine, agreeing with añjanīm and śalākām).

hindi: तब रात में विचरने वाले प्राणियों में से किसी एक की खोपड़ी को अञ्जन से भरकर, मरी हुई स्त्री की योनि में डालकर जलवाए।
english: Then, having filled the skull of any one of the night-roaming creatures with ointment (añjana) and inserted it in the vagina of a dead woman, one should have it burned.

text_flags.why: mṛtāyāḥ is genitive singular and needs striyāḥ; the final visarga looks lost

notes: añjana (ointment) is not said to be the one made in units 8 to 10, though context suggests it. 'it' (the filled skull) is supplied in English and implied in Hindi.

hindi: उस अञ्जन को पुष्य में निकालकर उस अञ्जनी में रखे।
english: Having taken out that ointment under Puṣya, one should place it in that añjanī.

hindi: उससे जिसकी आँखें लेपित हैं, वह नष्ट-छाया-रूप होकर विचरता है।
english: With that, with his eyes anointed, he moves about with his shadow-form lost.

words.gloss: who has set up the fire

words.gram: pres. pass. part. √dah, m. acc. sg.

hindi: जहाँ आहिताग्नि ब्राह्मण को जला हुआ अथवा जलता हुआ देखे, वहाँ तीन रात उपवास किया हुआ, पुष्य में, अपने आप मरे हुए के वस्त्र से थैली बनाकर, चिता की भस्म से भरकर, उसे बाँधकर, नष्ट-छाया-रूप होकर विचरता है।
english: Where one should see a brāhmaṇa who has set up the fire, burnt or being burnt, there, having fasted three nights, under Puṣya, having made a bag with the garment of one who has died of himself and having filled it with pyre-ashes and tied it on, he moves about with his shadow-form lost.
notes: svayaṃ-mṛta is literally 'dead by himself'; it may mean one who died a natural death (not killed). prasevaṃ = bag (the sense of prasevaka); medium confidence. āhita-agni: one who has installed the sacred fire. The Sanskrit does not say whose garment is 'one who has died of himself' (it may be the brāhmaṇa or another).

words.gloss: filled with powder of bones and marrow

hindi: ब्राह्मण के प्रेतकर्म में जो गौ मारी जाती है, उसकी अस्थि और मज्जा के चूर्ण से भरी साँप की थैली पशुओं से अन्तर्धान है।
english: A snake-bag filled with powder of the bones and marrow of the cow that is killed in the funeral rite of a brāhmaṇa is the concealment (antardhāna) from animals.
notes: Nominal sentence; 'is' is supplied. gaur is masculine (a bovine; 'cow' used). ahi-bhastrā: literally 'snake-bag', possibly a bag made of snake-skin; not decided. asthi-majja may also be read 'bone-marrow'. paśūnām antardhānam: genitive of the creatures from whom one is concealed ('concealment from animals'). In units 15 to 17 the classes paśu (domestic animals), mṛga (beasts) and pakṣin (birds) are named.

words.gloss: of one bitten by a snake

hindi: साँप के काटे हुए की भस्म से भरी प्रचलाक की थैली मृगों से अन्तर्धान है।
english: A pracalāka-bag filled with the ash of one bitten by a snake is the concealment from beasts (mṛga).
notes: pracalāka is obscure and kept as printed (the compound could be 'bag of pracalāka'; a kind of snake or other creature is possible, not stated). 'the ash of one bitten' is literally 'with the ash of the snake-bitten'. mṛga = beasts, deer, wild animals; 'beasts' used.

words.gloss: filled with powder of tail, dung and knee-bone of owl and vāgulī

hindi: उल्लू और वागुली की पूँछ, विष्ठा और घुटने की हड्डी के चूर्ण से भरी साँप की थैली पक्षियों से अन्तर्धान है।
english: A snake-bag filled with powder of the tail, dung and knee-bone of the owl and vāgulī is the concealment from birds.
notes: The compound can also be divided as 'owl; tail, dung and knee-bone of the vāgulī'; the reading 'of both creatures' is chosen. jānv.asthi is jānu-asthi (knee-bone).

hindi: इस प्रकार अन्तर्धान के आठ योग।
english: Thus, eight contrivances of concealment.

text_flags.why: possible: aṣṭau 'eight' needs a plural, yogāḥ; though an eight-part set could be taken as a collective singular

notes: yoga rendered 'contrivance' as in 12.4 of the glossary (here: a prescribed preparation). The count of eight is not checked against the preceding units here. The closing iti is rendered 'thus'.

hindi: “वैरोचन बलि की, शतमाय और शम्बर की, भण्डीरपाक, नरक, निकुम्भ और कुम्भ की भी मैं वन्दना करता हूँ।
english: “I salute Bali Vairocana, Shatamaya and Shambara, Bhandirapaka, Naraka, Nikumbha and Kumbha as well.
notes: A list of names (asura-like figures; the text calls none of them so here). Vairocana is the patronymic of Bali. śata-māya may be an epithet of Śambara ('Śambara of a hundred illusions') or a separate name; the ca after it points to two names, as in unit 43 where it is written śatamāyaṃ. bhaṇḍīra-pāka may be one name or two (Bhaṇḍīra and Pāka); kept as one, as printed. The opening quotation mark is the editors'; the quoted mantra runs on through the following units.

hindi: देवल और नारद की मैं वन्दना करता हूँ, सावर्णि-गालव की वन्दना करता हूँ। इनके अनुयोग से तुम्हारे लिए महान् स्वापन किया गया है।
english: I salute Devala and Narada, I salute Savarni-Galava. By the application of these, a great putting to sleep has been made for you.
notes: sāvarṇi-gālava is singular: it may be one person (Gālava, a Sāvarṇi) or two names fused; kept as printed. anuyoga = application, invocation (also 'enquiry'); 'application' chosen. te: 'for you' (dative sense) or 'your'. svāpana = causing to sleep.

hindi: जैसे अजगर सोते हैं और सेना के खल भी सोते हैं, वैसे ही वे पुरुष सोएँ जो गाँव में उत्सुक हैं।
english: Just as pythons sleep, and army-scoundrels sleep too, so let the men sleep who are curious in the village.
notes: camū-khala is obscure; camū = army, khala = base or wicked person (also 'threshing floor'), so 'army-scoundrels' is a literal guess; low confidence. ajagara = python (large snake). kutūhala = curiosity, eagerness; 'curious' chosen, alternative 'restless, agitated'.

hindi: हज़ार भण्डकों और सौ रथ-नेमियों के साथ मैं इस घर में प्रवेश करूँगा; बर्तन चुप बैठे रहें।
english: With a thousand bhaṇḍakas and a hundred chariot-rims I shall enter this house; let the vessels remain silent.

text_flags.why: possible: bhaṇḍaka is unattested to me and the line ends with bhāṇḍakāḥ; the two may be one word

notes: bhaṇḍaka is kept as printed and left untranslated (obscure). bhāṇḍaka is the diminutive of bhāṇḍa 'vessel, ware, goods'; 'vessels' is the literal sense, medium confidence (could be 'goods' or 'baggage'). ratha-nemi = chariot-rim, wheel-rim. sahasreṇa is an instrumental ('with a thousand').

words.gloss: in the worlds of the gods

hindi: मनु को नमस्कार करके, शुनक-फेलकों को बाँधकर; जो देव देवलोकों में हैं और मनुष्यों में जो ब्राह्मण हैं,
english: Having made obeisance to Manu, having bound the śunaka-phelakas; the gods who are in the worlds of the gods, and the brāhmaṇas among humans,
notes: śunaka-phelaka is obscure (śunaka 'dog, little dog'; phelaka may relate to 'leavings'); kept as printed and not translated; the printed -ḥ could be nominative (subject) or an object of baddhvā. The sentence continues in unit 24 (the relative ye ... is completed there by etebhyaḥ).

words.gloss: gone to the end of study

hindi: अध्ययन के पार पहुँचे हुए सिद्ध, और जो कौलास तपस्वी हैं; इन सब सिद्धों से तुम्हारे लिए महान् स्वापन किया गया है।
english: The siddhas who have gone to the end of study, and the kaulāsa ascetics: from these, all the siddhas, a great putting to sleep has been made for you.

text_flags.why: possible: 'ascetics of Kailāsa' would fit tāpasāḥ; kaulāsa is not a word I know

notes: kaulāsa is kept as printed (obscure). etebhyaḥ can be ablative ('from') or dative ('for'); 'from' chosen, as in 'by the application of these' in unit 20. The siddhas here are the perfected ones.

hindi: और पार जाते हुए, वे एकत्र होकर मुझसे दूर चले जाएँ।
english: And they go past; let them go away from me, assembled.
notes: Obscure and possibly corrupt: atigacchanti may be a verb ('they go past, transgress') or a neuter participle ('[things] going past'); the subject is not stated, and 'away from me' renders the locative mayi loosely ('in me'). Rendered literally; low confidence.

hindi: अलिते, वलिते, मनु को स्वाहा।
english: Alite, valite, hail to Manu!
notes: alite and valite are mantra words (vocative-looking) of no clear meaning; svāhā is the cry of offering.

hindi: इसका प्रयोग।
english: The application of this.
notes: Heading: the use of the mantra just given.

words.gloss: from the hand of a dog-cooker woman

hindi: तीन रात उपवास किया हुआ, पुष्य से युक्त कृष्ण-चतुर्दशी को, श्वपाकी के हाथ से विलख का खुरचन खरीदे।
english: Having fasted three nights, on the dark fourteenth joined with Puṣya, one should buy the scrapings of vilakha from the hand of a dog-cooker woman.
notes: vilakha is obscure and kept as printed. avalekhana = scraping, what is scraped off; 'scrapings' (the number is not marked). śva-pākī (feminine of śvapāka, 'dog-cooker') is the name of an outcaste class; kept literal. kṛṣṇa-caturdaśī = fourteenth tithi of the dark fortnight.

hindi: उसे उसके माषों के साथ टोकरी में रखकर असंकीर्ण दाह-स्थान में गड़वाए।
english: Having put it together with its māṣas in a basket, one should have it buried in an unmixed cremation ground.
notes: tan-māṣa = tat-māṣa: 'its māṣas', with tat taken as the scraping; māṣa is a bean or a small weight (not decided; low-medium). 'it' is supplied. asaṅkīrṇa ādahane could also be the compound asaṅkīrṇa-ādahane; asaṅkīrṇa 'unmixed' (alternatives: uncrowded, unfrequented). kaṇḍolikā = a basket (of cane).

hindi: दूसरी चतुर्दशी को निकालकर, कुमारी से पिसवाकर गोलियाँ बनवाए।
english: On the second fourteenth, having taken it out and had it ground with kumārī, one should have pills made.
notes: kumāryā is ambiguous: kumārī as a plant or drug name ('with kumārī'), or 'by a girl' (agent of the causative). Kept as 'kumārī'; the plant is not identified. 'it' (the buried item) is supplied. 'the second fourteenth' is literally dvitīyā caturdaśī, apparently the next one after the burying.

hindi: तब एक गोली को अभिमन्त्रित करके, इस मन्त्र से जहाँ फेंकता है, वहाँ उस सबको सुला देता है।
english: Then, having charmed one pill, wherever he throws it with this mantra, it puts all that to sleep.

text_flags.why: etena (instrumental) is needed with mantreṇa; units 33 and 42 read etena mantreṇa

notes: 'this mantra' is the one in units 19 to 26 (and its prescribed use); the subject of prasvāpayati (the pill) and 'it' are supplied. tat sarvam is literally 'all that'.

hindi: इसी विधि से साही के तीन-काल, तीन-श्वेत काँटे को असंकीर्ण दाह-स्थान में गड़वाए।
english: By this very procedure, one should have a porcupine's quill, trikāla and three-white (triśveta), buried in an unmixed cremation ground.
notes: śvāvidh is taken as porcupine (literally 'dog-piercer'); śalyaka = quill, spine. tri-kāla is obscure: 'three times' or 'three black (parts)' (kāla can mean black, matching tri-śveta 'three-white'); kept as 'trikāla'. kalpa = rule, procedure (as in units 28 to 31).

hindi: दूसरी चतुर्दशी को निकालकर, दाह-स्थान की भस्म के साथ जहाँ इस मन्त्र से फेंकता है, वहाँ उस सबको सुला देता है।
english: On the second fourteenth, having taken it out, together with the ashes of the cremation ground, wherever he throws it with this mantra, it puts all that to sleep.
notes: 'it' (the buried quill) and the subject of prasvāpayati are supplied. The e-text writes yatra.etena with '.', not '-'; read as two words.

hindi: “सुवर्णपुष्पी, ब्रह्माणी और ब्रह्मा, कुशध्वज की, सब देवताओं की मैं वन्दना करता हूँ, सब तपस्वियों की वन्दना करता हूँ।
english: “I salute Suvarnapushpi, Brahmani and Brahma, Kushadhvaja; I salute all deities, I salute all ascetics.
notes: Suvarṇa-puṣpī (literally 'golden-flowered') is kept as a name; it could also be a plant name. brahmāṇam read as Brahmā (alternative: 'a brāhmaṇa'). kuśa-dhvaja 'with a kuśa-grass banner' is kept as a name and may be an epithet of Brahmā.

hindi: ब्राह्मण मेरे वश में आएँ, और भूमि के पालक क्षत्रिय; वैश्य और शूद्र भी वश में आएँ, वे सदा मेरी वशता को प्राप्त हों।
english: Let the brāhmaṇas come under my control, and the earth-protectors, the kṣatriyas; let the vaiśyas and the śūdras also come under control, let them always come into subjection to me.
notes: bhūmi-pālāś ca kṣatriyāḥ: 'earth-protectors' and 'kṣatriyas' are taken in apposition; they could be two groups (kings and warriors). vaśam yāntu is idiomatic 'come under control/sway'.

hindi: स्वाहा! अमिले, किमिले, वयुचारे, प्रयोगे, फक्के, वयुह्वे, विहाले, दन्तकटके, स्वाहा!
english: Hail! Amile, kimile, vayucāre, prayoge, phakke, vayuhve, vihāle, dantakaṭake, hail!
notes: A string of mantra words, mostly without clear meaning, kept as printed. vayu-cāre may be 'moving in the vayu (wind?)' and danta-kaṭake literally 'tooth-bracelet/ring' (kaṭaka also 'camp'); not translated. prayoge is a real word ('in the application') but is taken here as one of the vocative mantra names. The dash '-' is a separate token in the e-text.

hindi: गाँव में जो उत्सुक कुत्ते हैं, वे सुख से सोएँ; और साही का यह तीन-श्वेत काँटा ब्रह्मा द्वारा बनाया हुआ है।
english: Let the dogs sleep comfortably, those that are curious in the village; and this three-white quill of the porcupine is made by Brahma.
notes: brahma-nirmita: brahma may be Brahmā or brahman (sacred power, the Veda); 'Brahma' chosen. 'Is' is supplied. kutūhala as in unit 21.

hindi: सब सिद्ध सो गए हैं; यह स्वापन तुम्हारे लिए किया गया है, जहाँ तक गाँव की सीमा का अन्त है, सूर्य के उदय तक।
english: All the siddhas are indeed asleep; this putting to sleep has been made for you, as far as the end of the village boundary, until the rising of the sun.
notes: Closing iti marks the end of the quoted mantra; it is not translated, and the quotation closes with the mark in unit 39. udgamanāt (ablative) is taken as 'until sunrise' (limit of time with yāvat); literal 'from the rising'.

english: Hail!”
notes: GROUPING: this one-word unit is the closing svāhā of the mantra of units 34 to 38; the closing quotation mark is part of the token. The quotation marks in unit 19 and 43 openings have no closing mark of their own in this chunk.

hindi: इसका प्रयोग।
english: The application of this.
notes: Heading: the use of the mantra just given.

words.gloss: having a hundred and eight sampātas

hindi: साही के तीन-श्वेत काँटे: सात रात उपवास किया हुआ, कृष्ण-चतुर्दशी को, खदिर की समिधाओं से, इस मन्त्र से अग्नि को एक सौ आठ सम्पात वाला करके, मधु और घी से होम करे।
english: The three-white quills of the porcupine: having fasted seven nights, on the dark fourteenth, with sticks of khadira wood, having made the fire one of a hundred and eight sampātas with this mantra, one should offer [them] with honey and ghee.
notes: Syntax uncertain. The quills are in the accusative/nominative plural and are taken as the things offered ('[them]' supplied). agnim ... aṣṭa-śata-sampātaṃ kṛtvā is literally 'having made the fire have 108 sampātas'; sampāta (here an act of the rite, possibly a repetition or a pouring, 'falling together') is kept untranslated. It may mean reciting the mantra 108 times over the fire. abhijuhuyāt = offer into/over (the fire). khādira: of khadira wood (a tree name, not identified).

hindi: तब एक को इस मन्त्र से गाँव के द्वार अथवा घर के द्वार पर जहाँ गाड़ा जाता है, वहाँ उस सबको सुला देता है।
english: Then one [quill], with this mantra, wherever it is buried at a village gate or a house door, puts all that to sleep.
notes: 'quill' and 'it' are supplied (ekam is neuter, agreeing with śalyaka). dvāri is the locative of dvār (door, gate).

hindi: “वैरोचन बलि की, शतमाय और शम्बर की मैं वन्दना करता हूँ; निकुम्भ, नरक, कुम्भ, तन्तुकच्छ और महान् असुर की भी।
english: “I salute Bali Vairocana, Shatamaya and Shambara; Nikumbha, Naraka, Kumbha, Tantukaccha, the great asura.
notes: Name list as in unit 19, in a different order (here Śatamāya is written as one word). mahā-asuram may be an epithet of Tantukaccha or a further figure; 'asura' kept.

hindi: अर्मालव और प्रमील, मण्ड-उलूक, घट-उबल, कृष्ण-कंस-उपचार, और यशस्विनी पौलोमी की भी।
english: Armalava and Pramila, Manda-uluka, Ghata-ubala, Krishna-kamsa-upachara, and the glorious Paulomi.
notes: Name list continuing units 19 and 43 (the verb vande is understood from unit 43). maṇḍa-ulūka, ghaṭa-ubala and kṛṣṇa-kaṃsa-upacāra are obscure compounds kept as names; the last could also be split into separate names (Kṛṣṇa, Kaṃsa-upacāra), not decided. Paulomī is the feminine patronymic of Puloman's family; only that is stated.
